title: Rejection: asking for feedback, and keeping the pipeline alive

videos.script: Most applications end in a no, and in a first job search that includes most of the ones you cared about. {{most}} A rejection after an interview hurts more than silence, because this time somebody met you. {{hurts}} It is also the one point in the process where you can ask for something useful: what to do differently next time. {{useful}} This lesson asks for feedback in a way people answer, reads what comes back, and keeps the rest of the search moving so that one no does not stop everything.
